realistic.label: realistic
realistic.goal: 写实版材质，风格不变（纹理突出，明暗随风格参考图）
realistic.scene: Images 1 to {views} are frames of one location in a 2.5D game, all seen from the same fixed camera angle while the camera travels over it; Image {look_image} is a style reference only. Build one large, complete overview picture of the whole area these frames cover, from the same camera angle, perspective and scale: every place, building, structure, path, water, terrain feature and fixed prop exactly where the frames show it relative to the others, joined into one continuous place, with nothing invented between them beyond a natural continuation of the ground. Convert everything into realistic materials while keeping the style unchanged, taking the materials, lighting, colour grading, brightness and texture detail from Image {look_image} and nothing else (none of its objects, layout, UI or text). Leave out characters, animals, moving vehicles, carried items, UI, HUD, numbers, icons, buttons, logos and all text: this is the empty location. Realistic materials of what is there (the list only describes materials, do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look} Clean and sharp, no heavy noise and no broken or fragmented artifacts. {extra}
realistic.subject: Image 1 is a close crop of {what} from a 2.5D game video ({description}); Image 2 is the whole frame it comes from; Image 3 is the same video's location already converted into realistic materials. Make a turnaround reference sheet of {what} only: three complete views side by side (front, side and back), the same size, on a plain light grey background, evenly lit, nothing cropped. Keep its shape, proportions, colours, markings, clothing, equipment and number of parts exactly as in Image 1; only convert its materials into realistic real-world materials with the style unchanged, at the realism, lighting quality and texture detail of Image 3. No text, labels, captions, logos or UI. {look}
realistic.video: Edit the video: replace the materials of the input video frame for frame; the output is the same video, only with realistic materials. At every moment keep exactly the input video's camera position, angle, zoom and framing: one continuous high top-down shot with the camera moving only as it moves in the input, never a cut, a close-up, a zoom-in or a camera move of your own. Convert every game-rendered cartoon material into realistic real-world materials while keeping the style unchanged. Keep every character's action, the position, size, shape and count of every object and the timing exactly as in the input video; do not add, remove or move anything, and nothing appears before it appears in the input video. {refs} Realistic materials of what is on screen (the list only describes materials, do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look} Keep on-screen UI numbers, icons and buttons exactly as they are. {remove}Do not add any new text, captions, watermarks or logos. No heavy noise and no broken or fragmented artifacts, no flicker; materials stay the same from frame to frame. {extra}
realistic.default_materials: realistic ground, water, ice and snow, wood, stone, metal, plants, cloth and character clothing
realistic.look: Overall look: real-world surface textures that stand out clearly (wood grain, bark, packed snow, ice, stone, rope fibres, fabric weave, fish scales), real light with natural shadows and contact shadows, crisp fine detail, clean. The ground matters most for realism: every ground surface (soil, packed and loose snow, ice, gravel, planks) has a complex, deep and finely detailed texture with uneven relief, grain, small stones, cracks, drifts and trodden marks, crisp into the distance; never a smooth, flat or uniform fill. Never pastel, glossy or cartoonish.

remove: Remove the {items} from the frame and fill the area naturally with the surrounding scene, leaving no trace; remove only these elements and keep all other text, numbers, signs and UI in the frame unchanged.
